status.nb: 114 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 20 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits continue to attack civilian communities in Zamfara, killing two clerics, abducting an 11‑month-old baby and other residents, while gunmen target Irigwe villages in southern Kaduna and around Kainji Lake. The Nigerian army has responded with ambushes that killed two bandits and recovered weapons, and police operations in Benue have arrested suspects linked to bandit and robbery networks. A 19‑year-old Christian farmer lost a hand in a separate attack, and a land dispute in Niger state sparked dozens of deaths. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter fortsetter å angripe sivile samfunn i Zamfara, dreper to prester, bortfører en 11‑måneder gammel baby og andre innbyggere, mens væpnede menn tar sikte på Irigwe-landsbyer i sørlige Kaduna og rundt Kainji-sjøen. Den nigerianske hæren har svart med bakholdsangrep som drepte to banditter og gjenvant våpen, og politiet i Benue har arrestert mistenkte knyttet til banditt- og røvernettverk. En 19‑år gammel kristen bonde mistet en hånd i et separat angrep, og en jordkonflikt i Niger-stat førte til dusinvis av dødsfall. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
